messages:
jess: FYI a customer (acct: acme-llc) reported that within a single chat session the model keeps flipping behavior. sometimes it answers concisely, other times it hallucinates details. Started after last night's rollout :thinking_face:
ryan_support: thanks for the ping — can you paste one example convo we can repro with? request_id if available helps.
jess: here's a short snippet and the request id: req=0x9f3aab. payload: `model=rw-3-8b`, `route=eu-west-1:low-latency`, conversation: 
```
User: summarize invoice #3245
System: (first response) Invoice 3245: total $12,345, paid via wire on 2026-02-10.
System: (second response) Invoice 3245: customer name "Acme Widgets", shipped items include widget A, widget B, tracking 1Z999... (these details are fabricated)
```
jess: Both replies came within ~2s of each other in same session. Customer says outputs are inconsistent and risky.
ryan_support: ugh. did they set any model variant pinning or caching? any reroute headers?
sanjay_eng: looking at logs for req 0x9f3aab — I see two serve events: one hit `variant=rw-3-8b-v1` then a second call routed to `variant=rw-3-8b-v1-quant` within same session. That smells like fallback routing during a capacity event.
maria_infra: ops-bot shows a canary swap at 2026-03-14T03:11:40Z right before the timestamp. Canary policy had `enable_fallback=true` for low-latency routes.
ops-bot: deploy: canary swap completed: rw-3-8b-v1 -> rw-3-8b-v1-quant (partial) (deploy_id: dpl-20260314-7) :white_check_mark:
ryan_support: so customer session got mixed variants mid-session. is sticky routing supposed to prevent that?
sanjay_eng: sticky routing should keep session-to-variant affinity for the session token, but our affinity window is 30s and only applies when `session_key` is provided. Their integration doesn't set a session_key — we default to per-request routing.
ryan_support: got it. can we confirm whether both variants have different tokenizer/decoder settings that could cause hallucination differences?
sanjay_eng: yes — the quantized variant uses a slightly different sampling temperature fallback and a patched decode table to save memory. In most cases outputs match, but rare divergence can happen in edge contexts (numbers, names).
jess: customer is requesting rollback or for us to guarantee consistent behavior. What's the recommended short-term mitigation?
alex_prod: quick options: 1) pin them to `rw-3-8b-v1` via the console (model pinning / route override) 2) ask infra to temporarily disable fallback for that route 3) recommend they set `session_key` so affinity holds. For long term we should tighten deploy fallbacks.
maria_infra: I can flip `enable_fallback=false` on that route for the tenant's org id (acme-llc) and roll that change within 5min. will do if support confirms.
ryan_support: do it, and I'll inform the customer. Also capture a minimal repro we can use for CI.
maria_infra: done — `enable_fallback=false` set on route eu-west-1:low-latency for org=acme-llc. change_id=chg-8392.
ops-bot: config: route update applied (chg-8392) by maria_infra at 2026-03-14T03:18:10Z :white_check_mark:
jess: customer confirmed after config change responses are stable and match historical behavior. they asked for a postmortem and a permanent fix.
sanjay_eng: follow-ups: (a) change default to require session_key for affinity opt-out, (b) add a pre-deploy check that compares variant decoding configs, (c) add a flag to force intra-session pinning during rollouts. I'll file tasks.
ryan_support: filing internal bug and CCing customer success for SLA note. thanks all. :thumbsup:
